findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how Tier-2 (Pass-1/frontier) establishes its parity baseline given that corpus `provider_provenance.ran_model` never records a frontier-class id, and define the fallback when no per-pass frontier baseline exists (e.g. pin against the configured production frontier class rather than the corpus ran_model).
evidence: Plan invariant 2: 'refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's provider_provenance.ran_model.'
Plan Tier 2 is Pass-1 replay with 'frontier Opus for Pass 1'.

Codebase fact (unknowable from plan text): provider_provenance.ran_model 'records whichever pass last touched the review's overall provenance (empirically always the standard class in this corpus, since no row records a frontier-class ran_model -- Pass-1's per-call model is not separately persisted per finding)' (src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier2.py:73-77).
corpus.py:287 populates a single row-level ran_model from provider_provenance.ran_model, confirming it is not per-pass.
findings.finding: Invariant 2's model-parity gate keys on the corpus baseline's `provider_provenance.ran_model`, but that field is single-valued per sidecar and records only the last-touching pass (never a frontier/Pass-1 model id); the plan specifies no way to establish or fall back for a frontier baseline, so the Tier-2 (Pass-1, Opus) parity check as written has no baseline to compare against.
findings.location: Approach → Non-negotiable invariants #2 (Model parity); AC line 'Every eval result records the per-pass model id; the harness … refuses to run a pass on a model other than its production class via Bedrock'
scenarios: A contributor runs a Tier-2 (Pass-1 / Opus) eval and the harness tries to enforce parity against a corpus baseline that carries only a standard/Sonnet ran_model, so the configured frontier model always 'differs' — either spuriously refusing every Pass-1 run or forcing the check to be silently skipped for Pass 1.
findings.suggested_fix: State that model parity is enforced PER PASS: Pass-2/Tier-1 diffs against the corpus `ran_model` (standard class), while Pass-1/Tier-2 pins against the configured production frontier class directly (there being no frontier `ran_model` in the corpus), and record the resolved per-pass model id in each result for the diff-refusal check.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'prompt caching confirmed active' AC and the Tier-2 Bedrock-Opus cost estimate with the repo's measured non-caching of Bedrock claude-opus-4-5 (bedrock-access.md, ADR 0059): scope the caching AC to Sonnet/Pass-2, or state Tier-2 runs uncached-but-correct with cost modeled accordingly.
evidence: Plan AC: 'Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call); verified from the usage log.'
Plan invariant 2: 'frontier Opus for Pass 1 ... through Bedrock only'

infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md:146-147 — 'Caching is model-dependent and fails silently ... Measured working: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6. Measured NOT caching: us./global. claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0.'

docs/adr/0059-...:975-978 — 'Bedrock does not straightforwardly "fix" the opus caching failure ... contradicted ... by cache_read=0/cache_write=0 on a Bedrock call and by non-caching us. and global. opus-4-5 profiles. The opus-4-5 datapoint is never reconciled.'
findings.finding: The plan makes an unresolved capability assertion: it mandates Bedrock-only frontier Opus for Pass-1 (invariant 2) and makes 'prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call)' a blanket acceptance criterion, but the repo's own authoritative sources record that Bedrock Opus (claude-opus-4-5) is measured NOT to cache — so the caching AC is likely unsatisfiable for Tier 2 and the Tier-2 cost model rests on an unreconciled premise.
findings.location: Approach → invariant 2 (Model parity) and Acceptance Criteria: 'Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call)'; also Tier 2 cost estimate ('Opus, ~$3.4/review uncached')
scenarios: A Tier-2 (Pass-1/Opus) run: the AC's 'cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call' check fails not because of a harness regression but because Bedrock Opus never caches, blocking sign-off or forcing the AC to be silently ignored for Tier 2.
Budget pre-flight: Opus calls bill full input on every call (no cache_read discount), so a caching-aware estimate under-projects Tier-2 spend against the $200 cap.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the caching invariant by pass: assert cache_read_tokens>0 only for Tier-1/Sonnet (measured caching), and for Tier-2/Opus explicitly note that Bedrock opus-4-5 is measured non-caching (per ADR 0059 §7 + bedrock-access.md), so the Tier-2 pre-flight estimate must use full uncached input pricing and the caching AC does not apply to Pass-1.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconstruct and include the ticket title in the corpus row and feed the exact production plan text (`title + '\n\n' + description`, via `shared_plan_prefix(plan_text)`) to both Tier-1 and Tier-2 re-runs; state how title-equivalence is established given the title is outside the `material_fingerprint` basis (e.g. record the at-review title from the reconstructed CREATE/EDIT state and assert it in the manifest).
evidence: Plan: 'The model re-run consumes the same normalized material the corpus builder reconstructs — normalized-basis equivalence is what the replay needs, not byte-exact text.'

Production: PlanContext.plan_text = f'{self.title}\n\n{self.description}' (det_floor.py:185-186); Pass-1 finder and Pass-2 verifier both embed prompts.shared_plan_prefix(plan_text) (passes.py:250/258, workflow_ops.py:365).
ABSENCE: material_basis (material_diff.py:134-143) hashes description/file_impact/children/reason but NOT the title — so fingerprint-equivalence does not establish title-equivalence.
Corpus: _reconstruct_material returns no title; _build_context sets title='' (corpus.py:207-227). Tier-1 replay_review calls verify_findings(context=row.get('description') or '') (tier1.py:157).
findings.finding: The LLM-replay tiers feed the verifier/finder a DIFFERENT plan text than production: production embeds prompts.shared_plan_prefix(PlanContext.plan_text) where plan_text is `title + '\n\n' + description`, but the corpus reconstructs no title (_build_context hardcodes title='') and Tier-1 passes only the bare `description` as context. Because the title is NOT part of the material_fingerprint basis, a row can be marked `verified` while its title is silently absent, so the model re-run does not consume the same material production judged.
findings.location: Approach — Tier 1/Tier 2; and Acceptance Criteria line 'at-review plan text reconstructed and material-fingerprint-equivalent'
scenarios: The Tier-1 reproduction run (shipped prompt vs stored answers) that the plan calls 'the Pass-2 noise floor' — a systematic missing-title divergence depresses agreement and is misattributed to reviewer noise, widening the noise band and hiding real prompt regressions.
Any plan whose title carries material scope the finding/verification depends on (e.g. a title naming the changed subsystem).
findings.suggested_fix: In corpus._reconstruct_material, replay the title from CREATE/EDIT `fields` the same way `description` is replayed, thread it through _build_context (title=<reconstructed>), and have Tier-1/Tier-2 build the verifier/finder context from the full PlanContext.plan_text rather than the raw description; since the title is not covered by the fingerprint, record it explicitly in the corpus row so a divergence is auditable rather than silent.
